target_customer: Large employers (banks, consultancies, consumer brands) that pay to build free job simulations used to attract and screen college students; students use it free.
problem: Students could not see what a job is really like before applying, and employers struggled to reach and assess candidates beyond a few target campuses.
business_model: B2B employer-paid sponsorship of free student job simulations, with recruiting and engagement services
product_category: Career education and early-talent recruiting platform

founders.name: Tom Brunskill
founders.background_notes: No background found in the YC page, TechCrunch or EAB release.

founders.name: Pasha Rayan
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as co-founder of Forage and later of A1Base (YC W25). No education or employers on the page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A content and learning web platform. The hard part in 2019 was producing employer-quality task content and partnerships, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: A library of branded employer simulations and a large student audience (more than 4 million per the YC page) was slow for rivals to build, but the format itself was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it in the sources found. The company was bought by EAB in April 2024, a higher-education services firm.

market_need_then: Employers spent heavily on campus recruiting and wanted broader, more diverse early-career pipelines, while students asked for internships at specific companies (TechCrunch 2020 describes students not using the original mentoring marketplace and asking for company-specific experience).

branding.domain_note: Operates at theforage.com, not the bare word domain.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission language about distributing opportunity (YC description)

rebrands.why: Announced with the Series A as the product moved from a mentoring marketplace to employer-built job simulations; TechCrunch gives no explicit naming reason.

branding.community_and_virality: University career centers widely list Forage as a recommended resource, and the site claims 9M+ sign-ups (company figure).

brand_strength.rationale: Recognized by students and career offices through employer-branded programs, but the brand leaned on partner logos; no source on press about the brand itself.

pivots.from: InsideSherpa mentoring marketplace for virtual work experience
pivots.to: Forage employer-built job simulations as a step before recruiting
pivots.why: Per TechCrunch, students were not using the mentoring marketplace as intended and kept asking for internships at specific companies.

outcome_analysis: Forage started in 2017 as InsideSherpa, pivoted away from a mentoring marketplace toward employer-built job simulations, rebranded in 2020, and raised a $9.3M Series A and a $25M Series B by August 2021. Remote hiring tailwinds and big-name employer partners gave it scale, and EAB agreed to acquire it in April 2024. The price was not disclosed, so whether the exit was a strong one is unknown.
notes: TechCrunch implies about $2.3M raised before the Series A (total known $11.6M); not labeled or itemized, so not recorded as a round. Aggregators give conflicting totals ($36.1M and $11.8M) and one claims 2026 rounds; unverified and excluded. No competitor source dated near early 2019 was found (a search returned only later university guides), so the list is empty. Series B date is the article publication date.
